after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3+7t \\ y=5t \\ z=1-5t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3+7t \\ 5t \\ 1-5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7t \\ 5t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(-3,0,1)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3+7t \\ y=5t \\ z=1-5t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3+7t \\ 5t \\ 1-5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7t \\ 5t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(-3,0,1)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5t-7 \\ y=-1-10t \\ z=\frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5t-7 \\ -1-10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5t \\ -10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-7,-1,\frac{3}{5})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].$

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5t-7 \\ y=-1-10t \\ z=\frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}

after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(3,-3,5)$ and $Q(7,2,1).$
after.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 5t \\ -4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3+4t \\ -3+5t \\ 5-4t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3+4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=5-4t\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(3,-3,5)$ and $Q(7,2,1).$
content.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 5t \\ -4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3+4t \\ -3+5t \\ 5-4t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3+4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=5-4t\end{aligned}
$$
